Article Title: '9/11 architects were not hiding in caves': India hits out at Pakistan at UN over terror safe havens
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday hit out at Pakistan at the UN Security Council, saying Islamabad had provided a "permissive environment" to the "architects" of the 9/11 attacks and continues to provide space and support to terror groups such as Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed.Speaking at a UN Security Council meeting, India's Permanent Representative P Harish recalled the 9/11 terror attacks in United States and said al-Qaida leaders Osama bin Laden and Khalid Sheikh Mohammed were eventually found in settled communities in Pakistan rather than "caves or badlands".“The international community supported the global campaign to counter terrorism in the wake of 9/11. Let us not forget, however, that al-Qaida's terror ecosystem established its strategic depth beyond Afghanistan through its affiliates,” Harish said.“The leaders of al-Qaida who conceived and directed these 9/11 attacks did not escape justice in the wilderness of some ungoverned frontier.”The Indian envoy also listed out the names of terrorists found in Pakistan.Bin Laden, who ordered and financed the 9/11 plot, was “tracked down and killed in a fortified compound within a settled, guarded community under Operation Neptune Spear”, he said.Mohammed, “the principal architect of the operation, was found sheltering in an ordinary residential house.Ramzi Binalshibh, who coordinated the hijacker cell after being denied a visa to join them, was sheltering in an urban centre,” Harish said.Senior al-Qaida operative Walid bin Attash, who helped select and prepare several hijackers, was captured separately, while Mustafa Ahmed al-Hawsawi, a key financial and logistical facilitator of the 9/11 operation, was also captured in Pakistan, he said."In each case, these were not fugitives hiding in caves or badlands, they were men who had long evaded detection. Draining this swamp that provided an enabling environment for such monsters of humankind to prosper is important," Harish said, in a thinly veiled reference to Pakistan.Harish also drew attention to what he described as an axis involving Pakistan, al-Qaida and terrorists targeting India."The same permissive environment that sheltered the architects of 9/11 has, in the years since, continued to provide space, support, and impunity to affiliates of al Qaida such as Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed and their like," he said.He said these groups continue to operate under different identities to evade the Council's sanctions, while their terror-training infrastructure continues to operate with impunity.The international community must act against the continued existence of such sanctuaries, he said, "to ensure that more such individuals are not thrust upon any country or its citizens and no one loses family and loved ones".Last week, as the world marked 25 years of the September 11 terror attacks perpetrated by al-Qaida, UN Security Council members, including Pakistan, visited the 9/11 memorial in Lower Manhattan.
Article Summary: India's Permanent Representative P Harish recalled the 9/11 terror attacks in United States. He said al-Qaida leaders Osama bin Laden and Khalid Sheikh Mohammed were eventually found in settled communities in Pakistan rather than "caves or badlands" Harish said these groups continue to operate under different identities to evade the Council's sanctions.

Article Title: 'We don't appreciate what we get for free': Omar Abdullah backs UPI fee rollout
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah backed Centre's decision to introduce 0.4 percent merchant discount rate on UPI payments above Rs 2,000, saying that "running a UPI system" is not cheap.While talking to reporters, Omar said that people don't appreciate what they "get for free.""Not everyone is charged. First of all, person-to-person money transfers are not charged. After that, individual consumers will not be charged unless they cross a certain ceiling limit. As far as I understand, running this UPI system is not cheap. It takes a lot of money to run it. And the truth is, we don't properly appreciate what we get for free," J&K CM said."The government should ensure that the general public is not charged these fees. If a company is charged, I have no objection because companies make good money through UPI anyway," he added.This comes after the opposition raised concerns over the rollout of UPI charges, alleging that the cost would ultimately be borne by common citizens.Earlier on Wednesday, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi targeted the centre and accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of putting a on every single person by “taxing UPI".“Modiji has a completely diff concept, he's neither left or right he has decided to completely lie down straight and in front of Donald Trump. He's put a tax on every single Indian person by taxing UPI and giving huge amount op money to the United States,” the former Congress president added.The new MDR will take effect from October 15. However, UPI payments between individuals, including transfers made to friends, will not be charged, according to the Centre.Responding to the critics and concerns over the new framework, the Union finance ministry said banks were asked to ensure merchants do not pass MDR charges on to customers. “UPI application providers are expressly prohibited from imposing platform fees or hidden charges".
Article Summary: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah backs Centre's decision to introduce 0.4 percent merchant discount rate on UPI payments above Rs 2,000. Article Text:
The public offering is a major step for NSE after its plans to list on the stock exchanges remained stuck. (Image for representative purpose only)

Here are 10 key facts about the NSE IPO:

NSE IPO Details

NSE Offer Second Largest IPO in India

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

NSE IPO: The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of National Stock Exchange of India (NSE), the country’s largest stock exchange by total turnover across the cash market and equity derivatives segments, has gone live today. The IPO is looking to raise up to Rs 22,569 crore through an offer for sale (OFS).As the IPO is completely an OFS, the money raised through the sale will go to the existing shareholders offering their shares. NSE itself will not receive any proceeds from the issue.The public offering is a major step for NSE after its plans to list on the stock exchanges remained stuck for almost a decade. The delay was linked to regulatory hurdles, including issues arising from the co-location controversy.NSE is positioned to gain from increasing retail participation in the capital markets. However, its earnings continue to depend substantially on transaction volumes.NSE’s post-issue price-earnings (P/E) multiple of 42.9 is lower than BSE’s 53, even though NSE holds a dominant position in the market.The IPO gives investors an opportunity to participate in a debt-free exchange business operating in a tightly regulated industry, where high entry barriers provide significant protection against new competition.The IPO consists entirely of an offer-for-sale, involving up to 12.64 crore equity shares being sold by existing shareholders. In terms of size, it is the second-largest public issue in India, behind Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870-crore IPO in 2024.NSE has set the price band at Rs 1,700-1,785 per equity share. At the upper end of the band, the exchange will be valued at Rs 4.42 lakh crore, while the valuation at the lower end stands at Rs 4.2 lakh crore.Investors are required to bid for a minimum of 8 shares. At the upper end of the band, a retail investor would need Rs 14,280 for the minimum application.The size of the offering has been reduced from the earlier proposal to sell 14.9 crore shares. This has also brought the total issue size down from the initial estimate of around Rs 30,000 crore. Based on the price band, the IPO is worth around Rs 21,494 crore at the lower end and approximately Rs 22,569 crore at the upper end.Even after the reduction in size, the NSE IPO has exceeded LIC's Rs 21,000-crore issue from 2022. It remains smaller than Hyundai Motor India's record-setting offering.A day before the IPO opened, NSE had raised Rs 6,746 crore from anchor investors. The anchor book included state-owned Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), Goldman Sachs and Fidelity.Sovereign wealth funds GIC Singapore, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) and Norges Bank also took part in the anchor allocation, along with Eastspring and HSBC Global Asset Management.The issue involves 23 existing investors, including State Bank of India, Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, Aranda Investments, The New India Assurance Company, SBI Capital Markets and Bank of Baroda.NSE was incorporated in 1992 and runs a vertically integrated market infrastructure platform spanning trading, clearing, listing, settlement, market data and index licensing.Its trading offerings include cash equities, mutual funds, commodity derivatives, equity futures and options, exchange-traded currency derivatives, wholesale debt and interest-rate futures.The exchange maintained a dominant position across key segments in FY26. It accounted for nearly 93% of the cash market, 99.7% of equity futures and 68.5% of equity options premium turnover.Transaction charges continue to provide the bulk of NSE’s revenue, but the exchange has also expanded into connectivity, colocation, data and licensing services. Revenue from these segments climbed 9.5% year-on-year to Rs 1,955.9 crore in FY26, contributing 11.8% of operating revenue.As of June 30, 2026, NSE had 132.4 million unique registered investors, 1,328 trading members and 3,005 listed entities. Despite this broad network, trading activity remains concentrated among a small number of participants. The top 10 trading members contributed 46.8% of FY26 revenue from operations.The exchange also faces risks from weaker trading volumes, regulatory changes in derivatives, technology failures, cyber risks and potential delays in executing its diversification plans, according to an ET analysis.NSE’s revenue increased at an annual rate of 6% over the preceding three years, but declined 3% year-on-year to Rs 16,601 crore in FY26. The main reason was a 4% reduction in transaction-charge revenue, which fell to Rs 13,057 crore as activity in the cash market, futures and options segments moderated following regulatory changes.Its operating margin before depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda margin) stood at 66.9% in FY26, compared with 66.8% in FY24. The margin was also above BSE’s 64% in FY26.Net profit, meanwhile, rose 11% annually to Rs 10,302 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 8,305.7 crore in FY24. Return on equity declined to 33% in FY26 from 37% in FY24, while BSE reported a higher return on equity of 45%.NSE has no debt and held a net cash position of Rs 17,976 crore as of March 31, 2026.Investors are valuing India’s largest stock exchange at nearly $46 billion, or about Rs 4.42 lakh crore, at the upper price band of Rs 1,785.At 42.9 times FY26 earnings, NSE commands a higher P/E multiple than most major listed exchanges, including Nasdaq, CME Group, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), LSEG, HKEX and SGX, according to analysts.NSE’s estimated market value of $46 billion compares with $54 billion for Nasdaq, $99 billion for CME, $88 billion for ICE, $82 billion for LSEG, $67 billion for HKEX and $14 billion for SGX. Its FY26 revenue, however, is estimated at $1.95 billion, significantly below Nasdaq’s $5.2 billion, CME’s $6.1 billion, ICE’s $10 billion and LSEG’s $12.1 billion.NSE’s profitability is a key factor behind its valuation. Its estimated net margin of about 55% is close to CME’s 57% and HKEX’s 59%, and higher than Nasdaq’s 34%, ICE’s 30%, LSEG’s 20% and SGX’s 47%.The subscription window will remain open until September 21. The stock is expected to be listed on September 24.NSE's grey market premium remained near 7% before the IPO opened, reflecting moderate expectations for the listing. While the GMP points to a positive mood among unlisted-market participants, it does not indicate the kind of aggressive premium that is often associated with smaller issues. With the offer being large and the valuation already elevated, the potential for listing gains could remain measured.Transaction charges contributed nearly 79% of operating revenue in FY26, with options alone accounting for nearly 60%. This leaves earnings exposed to regulatory changes, competitive pressures and fluctuations in stock market activity. Against this backdrop, the issue appears more suited to long-term investors who are comfortable taking on higher risk, according to an ET analysis.With NSE valued at 42.9 times FY26 earnings, the IPO does not come at a low valuation. The company's performance is also closely linked to trading activity, particularly in options. The 7% GMP points to demand in the unlisted market, but does not suggest an overwhelming level of enthusiasm.Brokerages have largely maintained a positive view of the issue. Analysts see the IPO as an opportunity for long-term investors to gain exposure to India's dominant market infrastructure company. Strong margins, a debt-free balance sheet, leadership in the market and an expanding investor base are among the factors supporting the long-term case.At the same time, valuation and regulatory risks remain important considerations.Angel One has a Subscribe call on the IPO. “At the upper price band of Rs 1,785, NSE is valued at a post-issue P/E of 35.4x, compared with BSE’s P/E of 54.2x, making the issue attractive relative to its key listed peer. NSE’s dominant market position, significantly higher revenue and profitability, strong market share in equity derivatives, and long-term structural growth in Indian capital markets provide further comfort,” the brokerage says.“Despite near-term regulatory headwinds to derivatives volumes, we believe the valuation offers a favourable entry point given the company’s strong competitive position and earnings potential. We recommend Subscribe for the IPO,” it adds.LKP Securities has assigned a "Subscribe" rating, putting the implied post-issue market capitalisation in the range of Rs 4.2 lakh crore to Rs 4.42 lakh crore.YES Securities has also recommended "Subscribe". The brokerage said NSE is being offered at a 21% discount to BSE on a price-to-earnings basis. According to YES Securities, BSE is valued at 54.3 times FY26 diluted earnings, compared with NSE's 42.9 times valuation at the upper end of the price band.
Article Summary: The public offering is a major step for NSE after its plans to list on the stock exchanges remained stuck for almost a decade. The delay was linked to regulatory hurdles, including issues arising from the co-location controversy. The IPO consists entirely of an offer-for-sale, involving up to 12.64 crore equity shares being sold by existing shareholders.

Article Title: E-waste from govt offices may fetch Rs 10,000 cr a year: MoS Jitendra Singh
Article Text:
Union MoS Jitendra Singh speaks during the launch of the Special Campaign 6 Monitoring portal to track the implementation of the campaign aimed at institutionalising Swachhata and reducing pendency across government offices, in New Delhi. (Photo: ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Launching the dedicated web-portal for the sixth edition of govt’s ‘special campaign’ to declutter govt offices, minister of state for personnel Jitendra Singh on Wednesday said the focus will henceforth shift to responsible disposal of non-functional electronic items lying in govt offices, with annual earnings from e-waste recycling expected to touch Rs 10,000 crore in a few years.According to secretary, ministry of mines, Keshav Chandra, e-waste has become the most valuable commodity as an input for the industry. E waste, when crushed together, generates ‘black mass’, which contains 30% of critical mineral requirements. This is the reason why most advanced economies of the world have the export of black mass. “Instead of going outside seeking critical minerals, we can obtain them from e-waste recycling,” Chandra said, adding that ‘Special Campaign 6’ will serve the dual purpose of removing garbage from govt offices and obtaining value from it.The ‘special campaign’ initiative to free up space and institutionalise cleanliness across govt offices was launched in 2021 and runs each year between the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi’s on Oct 2 to that of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on Oct 31. Over the years, the swachata initiative and special campaign have helped free up over 1,000 lakh square feet of office space, led to weeding out or closure of around 2 crore files and generated a revenue of Rs 5,103 crore from scrap disposal.“These achievements reflect the expansion of swachhata campaign beyond cleanliness to efficient utilisation of govt resources, reduction of pendency, better use of public spaces and conversion of waste into wealth,” Singh said while addressing mediapersons at the launch of Special Campaign 6.Secretary for the department of administrative reforms and public grievances (DARPG) Nivedita Shukla Verma said the govt will ensure that e-waste collected during the special campaign is handed over only to registered recyclers and disposed of in an environmentally sound manner.As many as 58 big recyclers have already registered to process the e-waste, according to Chandra.The govt had last year run a limited campaign for e-waste collection across 58 locations, placing bins in govt offices to collect non-functional and unused computers, keyboards, printers, laptops etc. The response encouraged the govt to make e-waste collection and recycling a critical component of Special Campaign 6.
Article Summary: MoS Jitendra Singh said the focus will henceforth shift to responsible disposal of non-functional electronic items lying in govt offices. Annual earnings from e-waste recycling expected to touch Rs 10,000 crore in a few years. ‘Special Campaign 6’ will serve the dual purpose of removing garbage and obtaining value from it.

Article Title: Xi suffered stroke & fainted at Brics Summit, claims China Democracy Party chief; post gets community note
Article Text:
Xi fainted at Brics summit, returned to China for treatment, claims Wanjun Xie

Wanjun Xie, chairman of the China Democratic Party, has claimed in a post on X that Chinese president Xi Jinping fainted during the Brics summit hosted by New Delhi and was taken back to China on a special flight for medical treatment.Xie claimed that after receiving emergency treatment from his accompanying medical team, Xi ended his visit to India early and returned to China on a special plane.According to the post, upon the plane's arrival at Beijing airport, authorities did not arrange for a large group of officials to greet Xi or organise a welcome ceremony. Instead, "a military helicopter was used to transport Xi Jinping directly to Beijing's 301 Hospital for emergency treatment."Xie further claimed that an expert team at Beijing's 301 Hospital diagnosed Xi with "a severe ischemic stroke, that is, a transient cerebral infarction."The post also claimed that Xi "feared that the Indian side might obtain information about his health" and therefore "refused emergency treatment at an Indian hospital" before returning to Beijing for care.According to Xie, "During the flight, as there were no conditions for surgery, the medical team could only administer conservative treatment to sustain Xi Jinping's life."He further claimed that Xi "missed the golden window for emergency care and surgery."The post alleged that even if Xi undergoes surgery at Beijing's 301 Hospital, "there is a high likelihood of severe sequelae."Xie also claimed that "the Beijing authorities are still unable to confirm whether Xi Jinping can recover his health before the visit to the United States", adding that authorities were waiting to determine whether it would be necessary to cancel Xi's planned late-September trip to the US.The post on X also carried Community Notes. The claims about Xi's alleged medical condition, treatment and possible US trip cancellation were presented as claims and were not independently established in the post.India hosted the Brics Summit on September 12-13, which was attended by leaders of the 11 member countries and 10 partner countries, along with representatives of international organisations. On the sidelines of the summit, Xi held bilateral talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, during which he presented Beijing’s proposals for greater cooperation among Global South countries.
Article Summary: Wanjun Xie, chairman of the China Democratic Party, has claimed in a post on X that Chinese president Xi Jinping fainted during the Brics summit hosted by New Delhi. Article Title: 'Committed to ensuring energy security': India reacts as 100% Trump tariff looms
Article Text: NEW DELHI: India on Thursday reacted to the passage of a new bill in United States that allows the Trump administration to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on countries buying crude oil from Russia and Iran. The ministry of external affairs, in a statement, said that New Delhi remains committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people."The government of India has noted the passage of the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act in the US Congress. We are monitoring further developments on this matter. As stated on several earlier occasions, India remains firmly committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people. It will continue to do so through diversified sourcing and on the basis of evolving market dynamics," it said."This issue has been discussed at high levels in recent months with various US interlocutors. Its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side," it added.The ministry further said that New Delhi will take "all necessary measures" to protect its trade and economic interests."Government will work closely with Indian trade and industry bodies to deal with the implications of these developments," it said.This comes after the 'Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026' was passed in the US House of Representatives. The legislation gives President Donald Trump the power to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on major buyers of Russian oil and gas, including India.The new Act allows the creation of a new legal route for Washington to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on Indian imports over New Delhi’s continued purchases of Russian energy.India and China are among the biggest buyers of Russian crude, and the tariff provision is intended in part to put pressure on countries that continue to support Russia's energy revenues.The measure directs the president to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on the five largest importers of Russian oil or natural gas. It includes an exception for countries that import less than 15 per cent of Russia's natural gas exports and have taken significant steps to reduce those purchases.
Article Summary: New Delhi remains committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people. The ministry of external affairs said that New Delhi will take "all necessary measures" to protect its trade and economic interests. This comes after the 'Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026' was passed in the US House of Representatives.

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday summoned Pakistan’s top diplomat in New Delhi and lodged a strong protest over the “unacceptable and unprofessional conduct” of Pakistani naval units that led to a collision with an Indian Navy vessel in international waters.“While the incident, which took place in international waters, did not cause any major damage, the conduct of the Pakistani naval ship was in direct contravention of Article 10 of the Agreement between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Manoeuvres and Troops Movements of April 1991,” the MEA said in a statement.The ministry said the Pakistani Charge d’Affaires was advised to convey to the concerned authorities that all military units must exercise due care and comply with relevant agreements between the two countries.“The Charge d'Affaires of Pakistan was advised to convey to the concerned Pakistani authorities, the need for all military units to observe due care and respect the provisions of the relevant agreements between the two sides in order to prevent any repeat of such incidents,” it said.The MEA also said India’s Charge d’Affaires in Islamabad had been instructed to lodge a similar protest with Pakistan’s ministry of foreign affairs.This is not the first time Indian and Pakistani ships have come into close contact in the Arabian Sea.In 2011, a diplomatic row had erupted over the MV Suez episode, then Navy chief Admiral Nirmal Verma said Pakistani warship PNS Babur had come “much closer” than was prudent, damaging a helicopter net on INS Godavari. Article Title: SC pulls up govt for 'denying' disabled soldiers their benefits
Article Text:
SC junked over 270 appeals filed by govt against such soldiers

NEW DELHI: Quoting Raksha Mantri 2015 Report, which admitted that "many disabled soldiers in India are still denied disability benefits on hyper-technical reasons", Supreme Court has pulled up Centre and the defence ministry for litigating against them in all forums of the judiciary - from tribunals to HCs and SC. It also highlighted that govt filed appeals after a long time in most of the cases.A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe noted that Raksha Mantri Report had recommended the immediate withdrawal of appeals pertaining to disability and pensionary benefits pending against soldiers with disabilities but said the recommendation had not been faithfully implemented. "Appeals such as these are filed and continue to be filed, even after the ministry of defence accepted the committee's recommendation for withdrawal of this class of litigation," the bench said, junking over 270 appeals filed by govt.The bench also examined the outcome of such cases in different judicial forums."The sad part of this litigation is that, out of around 271 civil appeals and special leave petitions, most of them are barred by limitation. Many similar appeals that were barred by limitation have already been dismissed in the past; the present batch is only a small number that survive. Moreover, it is significant to note that the number of appeals rejected at the first appellate stage, after a dismissal by the release medical board, far exceeds those accepted," SC said.According to information obtained under RTI Act, of the 2,997 appeals before the first appellate authority, 2,855 were rejected and only 142 appeals were accepted, the bench added. Before the second appellate authority, out of 456 appeals, 439 were rejected and only 17 accepted.The court examined Entitlement Rules 2008, passed in 2010 to replace the 1982 rules, and did not find any error in them. The 1982 Rules clearly create a presumption that if a member of the service is in sound physical and mental health at the time of entrance, then any disability at the time of discharge would be attributable to military service. The 2008 Rules, however, withdraw this presumption by adding a causal connection requirement. They say, "Mere fact that a disease has manifested during military service does not per se establish attributability to or aggravation by military service."The bench upheld the new rules, saying, "The mere addition of a causal requirement and a removal of the presumption that when a member joins service healthy, and, if, he leaves with a disability, it ought to be attributable to the military service, does not, by itself, change the core scheme of the Entitlement Rules 2008 because the other beneficial provisions broadly remain untouched. The onus to prove that the member's disability is not attributable to service still lies on the employer. The relevant rules regarding attributability and aggravation continue to hold that if cause of disability is unknown,... then the disability is attributable to service."
Article Summary: Supreme Court pulls up Centre and the defence ministry for litigating against them in all forums of the judiciary. It also highlighted that govt filed appeals after a long time in most of the cases. SC junked over 270 appeals filed by govt against such soldiers.

Article Title: Sleeping too little, or too much, could speed up aging
Article Text:
Researchers analysed data from about 5,00,000 UK Biobank participants and examined 23 biological aging clocks

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Sleeping too little, or even too much, may be linked to faster biological aging and a higher risk of death, according to a large study of nearly 5 lakh adults aged 37 to 84 years. People sleeping less than six hours had a 50% higher hazard of death from any cause, while those sleeping more than eight hours had a 40% higher hazard, compared with six to eight hours.The study, published in Nature, did not establish that sleep extremes directly cause earlier death or faster aging.Researchers analysed data from about 5,00,000 UK Biobank participants and examined 23 biological aging clocks based on magnetic resonance imaging, plasma proteins and metabolic markers. They found a U-shaped relationship between sleep duration and biological age gaps. The lowest gaps were generally recorded between 6.4 and 7.8 hours, depending on organ and sex. Among clocks showing a significant relationship, the lowest gaps occurred between 6.5 and 7.8 hours for women and 6.4 and 7.7 hours for men. The pattern was significant in 9 of 23 clocks, involving the brain, heart, lungs, liver, immune system, skin, endocrine system, fat tissue and pancreas."Sleep is not just about duration. Timing, depth and continuity also matter. There is no single ideal number of hours for everyone. Consistently sleeping too little or too much, particularly less than six or more than 9 hours, may indicate non-restorative sleep or an underlying sleep disorder, which can raise cardiovascular and metabolic risks and affect healthy aging," said Dr J C Suri, director and head, department of pulmonary, critical care and sleep medicine, Sitaram Bhartia Institute of Science and Research.The study identified 153 significant associations between abnormal sleep duration and future disease outcomes. Short sleep had broad links with mental health, metabolic, cardiovascular, pulmonary and digestive diseases. Researchers suggested disrupted sleep and circadian rhythms may affect inflammatory, metabolic, vascular, hormonal and tissue-repair pathways. Questions remain about young people's exposure to irregular schedules, artificial night light, late-night eating, shift work and "social jet lag". Sleep duration was self-reported, and sleep quality, interruptions, timing, architecture or regularity were not measured.
Article Summary: Researchers analysed data from about 5,00,000 UK Biobank participants. They found a U-shaped relationship between sleep duration and biological age gaps. The lowest gaps were generally recorded between 6.4 and 7.8 hours. Short sleep had broad links with mental health, metabolic, cardiovascular, pulmonary and digestive diseases.

NEW DELHI: Unhappy with a Jodhpur labour court award, a health worker from Jalore district, Rajasthan, engaged on a daily wage basis and whose services were terminated in 1999 had moved Rajasthan HC in 2004.The petition is yet to be heard, 22 years later.With pendency in HCs crossing the 65 lakh mark, there is a steady stream of petitions before the Supreme Court pleading for directions to the HCs concerned, not for expeditious adjudication of their grievance but for early hearing on their petitions after prolonged wait for justice. Nearly 15 lakh such cases have remained pending in HCs for over a a decade.Most applications come from Allahabad HC and Rajasthan HC, where the pendency of cases is 12.5 lakh and 7 lakh respectively.In Allahabad HC, each judge/bench takes up an average of 150-200 cases every day for hearing, but the monstrous pendency appears to be overwhelming the judicial decision-making capacity. Compared to Bombay and Madras HCs, the HCs of Delhi and Calcutta have relatively low pendency of cases at 1.2 lakh and 1.9 lakh cases.

Article Title: Good El Nino? How a bad monsoon left Delhi drenched
Article Text:
Delhi had a season’s rainfall surplus of 8% in a meteorological subdivision (Haryana)

Wet capital

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The capital defied the odds this monsoon. As of Sept 16, Delhi had a season's rainfall surplus of 8% in a meteorological subdivision (Haryana) that's reeling under a 23% deficit and a region (northwest India) that has logged a 10% shortfall. The season's peculiar rainfall pattern indicates that a strengthening El Nino as well as climate change may have played a role in giving the capital an unlikely monsoon bounty.A look at the season's district-level rainfall map of the region shows Delhi literally at the edge of the good monsoon zone this year (see graphic). Just north of the capital lies a swathe of deficient districts starting with neighbouring Sonipat (-32%) and Rohtak (-47%) and all the way up to Hoshiarpur (-53%) and Kapurthala (-69%) in Punjab - a cluster of over 30 rain-starved districts in Haryana and Punjab as well as adjoining Rajasthan, Himachal and west UP.So how did Delhi turn into a wet pocket next to a rain-deficient region? The answer lies in the way low-pressure systems coming from Bay of Bengal shifted direction this season, probably under the influence of El Nino, and how their interactions with westerly disturbances uniquely aided rains in Delhi-NCR.A majority of monsoon rainfall in northwest and central India happens under the influence of moisture-laden low-pressure systems (LPSs), including depressions, travelling inland from Bay of Bengal.Contrary to what one would expect, the number of such systems does not decrease in an El Nino year. In fact, a 2024 study in Climate Dynamics showed that the number of Bay of Bengal depressions increased in El Nino years in the 1979-2020 period, averaging 3.9 during July-Aug versus 2.4 in normal years.This year there were 10 LPSs, including four depressions in July-Aug, against a normal of less than nine.What generally changes in an El Nino year is the direction of the LPSs. "In El Nino years, there is subsidence of air over south India and its adjoining northern parts. This prevents formation of LPSs in the southern latitudes, say in central Bay of Bengal, which would normally move towards the north Andhra-south Odisha coast," said IMD director general Mrutyunjay Mohapatra.Here's where Delhi benefited, particularly in Aug, when as many as six LPSs, including two depressions, impacted India. With a northward shift, most of these systems entered inland over north Odisha-Bengal and tracked north-northwest, affecting Odisha, Bengal, Jharkhand, UP, Uttarakhand and the Delhi region, with lesser impact in Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab.There was another factor in play, likely linked to climate change. WDs are moist wind systems moving east from the Mediterranean region that usually bring wet weather to north India in winter through early summer. Historically, WDs are rare during the monsoons as the jet stream, which causes the disturbance, typically migrates north of the Himalayas by April-May. However, in recent years, the jet stream has persistently been retreating late, a trend scientists attribute to global warming. This year, there were 16 WDs in the June-Aug period - eight in Aug alone, as per IMD.There were several instances of the easterly monsoon system interacting with a WD, intensifying rainfall over parts of north India, including Delhi. For instance, monsoon's onset over the capital on July 2 happened during an active WD spell. The heaviest rain spells in Delhi (July 8-9, July 29, Aug 7-8, Aug 25) occurred when both a monsoon system and a WD were simultaneously active in the region. These interactions also brought heavy rains in west UP and left a catastrophic footprint in the hills - the Bandipora (J&K) cloudburst, fatal flash floods in Chamba (HP) and forced closure of around 290 roads across HP and Uttarakhand - but don't appear to have majorly impacted Haryana and Punjab.
Article Summary: As of Sept 16, Delhi had a season's rainfall surplus of 8% in a meteorological subdivision (Haryana) That's reeling under a 23% deficit and a region (northwest India) that has logged a 10% shortfall. The season's peculiar rainfall pattern indicates that a strengthening El Nino as well as climate change may have played a role.

Article Title: CGHS 'family' expands, but contribution stays unchanged
Article Text:
On Sept 1, the eligibility criteria for CGHS was expanded to include married sons and brothers of scheme card holders who are critically or terminally ill

On Sept 7, the health ministry extended coverage of Central Govt Health Scheme (CGHS) to adopted sisters of scheme beneficiaries. On Sept 1, the eligibility criteria for CGHS was expanded to include married sons and brothers of scheme card holders who are critically or terminally ill. Over the years, the criteria for beneficiaries have been steadily expanded. Yet the contribution by the cardholder remains the same, unlike in health insurance where the addition of a beneficiary, especially an elderly or ill beneficiary, could entail a steep increase in the premium paid.According to the Sept 7 office memorandum, the ministry received references "regarding the eligibility of adopted sisters (i.e. sisters adopted by parents of a CGHS beneficiary) for inclusion as dependent family members under CGHS". The 'sisters' have to be legally adopted by the parents of CGHS beneficiary and have to satisfy the existing criteria of dependency (staying in the same house as the cardholder), income ceiling (not be earning more than Rs 9,000 per month plus the applicable dearness allowance) and marital status (i.e. be unmarried, divorced, abandoned or separated), as applicable to biological sisters.The coverage of sons and brothers of beneficiaries was earlier available only to unmarried dependents. There were also age limits of 25 for sons and 18 for brothers, except for those permanently disabled, who were covered for life. The office memorandum issued by the health ministry on Sept 1 spelt out that "marriage shall not constitute a ground for cessation of CHS/medical attendance facilities in respect of dependent son or brother covered under these provisions whether on account of critical/terminal illness or permanent disability. .."Also, the lifetime coverage would now also apply for "chronic, severe, critical or terminal illnesses resulting in substantial and continuing functional impairment or inability to earn a livelihood/self-sufficiency".The addition of critically terminally ill beneficiaries could have a major financial implication for the exchequer as there is no ceiling on the amount spent on CGHS beneficiaries. Since no health insurance would normally cover a critically or terminally ill person, this expansion is fortuitous for an ill person, but only if s/he has a parent or sibling who is a CGHS cardholder.For dependent daughters and sisters there has never been any age limit but the coverage stops once they get married or get a job with salary above the stipulated limit. Similarly, unmarried/divorced/abandoned/separated daughters and sisters have been eligible for coverage for life, provided they fulfilled the condition of dependency and income. Children and siblings are required to "normally reside" with the primary cardholder to qualify for benefits.
Article Summary: On Sept 1, the eligibility criteria for CGHS was expanded to include married sons and brothers of scheme card holders who are critically or terminally ill. The'sisters' have to be legally adopted by the parents of CGHS beneficiary and have to satisfy the existing criteria of dependency and income.

Article Title: India sees no growth in power sector CO2 emissions as clean energy rises: Report
Article Text:
A surge in clean energy in India has kept carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in check across the country

NEW DELHI: A surge in clean energy in India has kept carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in check across the country’s power sector, with no growth from the first half of 2024 to the same period in 2026, and this is the first time in more than 50 years that there has been no growth in coal power over a two-year period, found an analysis published by the UK-based Carbon Brief on Thursday.The analysis, done by Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) for Carbon Brief, underlined that coal power has not recorded growth during the period, even as overall electricity demand grew.It also noted that both oil and gas consumption, at the same time, have fallen across the nation for two years in a row, helping alleviate the shock of the Hormuz crisis. Emissions from oil and gas, in fact, fell by 7% year-on-year, extending a reduction that began in 2025, despite higher demand for road transport fuels.Nevertheless, the new six-monthly analysis shows that India’s emissions grew by 3.7% year-on-year in the first half of 2026, due to increases from steel, cement and other sectors. The analysis found that the carbon-intensive steel and cement emissions grew by 8% year-on-year, reaching a 23% share of India’s total CO2 in the first half of 2026.Flagging India’s performance, the report noted that clean energy met all of the 7% rise in the country’s electricity demand over the two years, adding 63 terawatt hours (TWh), equivalent to the total demand of Switzerland.India has added 77 gigawatts (GW) of solar in this two-year period, helping meet 60% of the rise in electricity demand overall, it added.Looking at the state-wise contribution that led to the clean-power shift in India, the report said Gujarat saw both the largest reduction in fossil-fuel generation and the largest expansion in clean power. After Gujarat, the largest increases in clean-power generation were seen in Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu, which also saw reductions in power generation from fossil fuels.The report suggested that if the pace of India’s clean-energy expansion is to continue, it will need to upgrade its electricity grid, rapidly build out energy storage and boost the flexibility of coal power.The analysis, based on official monthly data for fuel consumption, industrial production and power generation from different ministries and govt institutes, shows that though clean-energy expansion is covering most or all of India’s power-demand growth, the fossil-fuel industry continues to pursue major capital investments.
Article Summary: A surge in clean energy in India has kept carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in check across the country’s power sector. No growth in coal power over a two-year period, found an analysis published by the UK-based Carbon Brief. Oil and gas consumption, at the same time, have fallen across the nation for two years in a row.

NEW DELHI: CBI has filed an FIR and launched a probe into an illegal funding network operated by US-based Christian missionary organisation, The Timothy Initiative, and its Indian leadership for allegedly using foreign funds to the tune of over 92 crore between Nov 2025 to April 2026 for missionary activities in violation of Foreign Contribution Regulation Act The agency's probe has also revealed that the cash withdrawals were deployed across India to conduct training programmes, preaching, and the targeted indoctrination of economically marginalised groups, which,CBI said, fostered left-wing extremism.CBI kicked off the probe following directions and approval from MHA. Key individuals named in the conspiracy include India operations head Jonathan S Rajan, primary financial handler Micah Mark, Ajit Verghese Mathai, along with field operatives Varghese Chacko, Bablu Kurmi, and Supreme Joy.CBI alleged the syndicate conspired to systematically channel foreign funds into India without oversight.The FIR, registered on the basis of findings shared by ED, says that the syndicate circumvented formal banking channels by distributing over 1,000 foreign debit cards issued by the US-based Truist Bank across India. Operatives systematically withdrew physical cash from ATMs in states such as Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, and Assam.Investigators estimate that between Nov 2025 and April 2026 alone, the network illegally funnelled $9,995,240 into the country. This came in addition to an earlier illicit withdrawal of Rs 44 crore executed through identical ATM transactions between Jan 2024 and March 2026.The trail unravelled after agencies intercepted Micah Mark at Bengaluru airport on April 18, 2026. Mark was caught carrying 24 Truist Bank debit cards, all fraudulently embossed with the single alias "Santosh Kumar.""This was allegedly orchestrated on the instructions of Ajit Verghese Mathai to bypass Know Your Customer mandates and conceal the identity of the real users. Investigations revealed Mark had made multiple overseas trips to bring back such debit cards. Following the raids, TTI USA attempted to tamper with evidence by blocking domestic access to its website (ttiglobal.org) and remotely wiping cloud servers with data stored on seized laptops," the FIR says.This amounted to destruction of evidence as it happened even as search and seizure proceedings were underway, officials said.Rajan managed training logistics, trainer selection, and venue identification while submitting financial requirements to the organisation's finance team to secure illegal overseas transfers. Field functionaries handled cash distribution after making regular ATM withdrawals.The I-T department carried out searches and seizures on the outfit earlier this year.
Article Summary: CBI has filed an FIR and launched a probe into an illegal funding network operated by US-based Christian missionary organisation, The Timothy Initiative. The organisation allegedly used foreign funds to the tune of over 92 crore between Nov 2025 to April 2026 for missionary activities.

Article Title: Hospitals could be charging you 2,841% higher on commonly used consumables
Article Text:
The issue has been flagged multiple times over last 15 years but a fresh push by Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has revived a question that has remained unresolved for years: who ultimately sets price of a medical device - the manufacturer, the hospital or the regulator?

How the prices are changed

NEW DELHI: An IV infusion set priced in the wholesale market for Rs 11 carries an MRP of Rs 325, while a disposable syringe available for under Rs 7 has a price tag of around Rs 60, putting a spotlight on one of the least visible components of hospital bills: the price of widely used consumables during treatment. The gap becomes even more stark for high-value devices such as pacemakers, heart valves and intraocular lenses, where the final MRP may be 10-30 fold higher than the import landed price.Such huge mark-ups ultimately inflate the patient's hospital bill and may add significantly to the out-of-pocket treatment cost.The issue has been flagged multiple times over last 15 years but a fresh push by Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has revived a question that has remained unresolved for years: who ultimately sets price of a medical device - the manufacturer, the hospital or the regulator?Several earlier analyses by National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) of hospital bills had shown how certain private hospitals procured consumables at rock-bottom prices but charged patients the high printed MRP, sources told TOI.Flagging mark-ups as high as 2,841% on commonly used hospital consumables, Tukaram Mundhe, Maharashtra FDA commissioner, posted on X on Tuesday, "The regulatory gap is structural: scheduled medicines are capped under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013. Most medical devices and consumables are not, leaving both the pricing and the information around it almost entirely unmonitored.'' He urged the Centre to frame guidelines to address the "permissible gap between trade procurement price and declared MRP".Nearly a decade ago, prices for cardiac stents and orthopaedic knee implants were capped by NPPA. And, in 2020, govt capped trade margins on certain critical items, including pulse oximeters, blood pressure monitors and glucometers, during the Coronavirus pandemic.Historically, the industry - domestic and MNCs - have been split over the capping of trade margins. The domestic industry represented by AiMeD cautioned that the current regulatory framework under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013, is inadequate to address the pricing of medical devices and has proposed capping trade margins at 75% for widely used consumables such as syringes and IV sets, and at 50% for high-value devices such as pacemakers and heart valves."Genuine device manufacturers and importers are at a clear disadvantage under the current system of unchecked hospital mark-ups. Ethical suppliers price their products transparently, based on ex-factory or landed import price, but when hospitals inflate MRPs by 10-30 times, the market rewards those willing to play the distortion game. Responsible companies that refuse to indulge in excessive margins are forced out of competition or in order to survive, have to comply with these unfair demands,'' said Rajiv Nath, forum coordinator, AiMeD, saidAs against this, Medical Technology Association of India, which represents MNCs, said it concurred with Maharashtra FDA Commissioner's "three asks of margin rationalisation, an inter-agency review and clear guidelines governing the permissible gap between trade procurement costs and declared MRPs", which is the "essence of Trade Margin Rationalisation".
Article Summary: An IV infusion set priced in the wholesale market for Rs 11 carries an MRP of Rs 325. A disposable syringe available for under Rs 7 has a price tag of around Rs 60. The gap becomes even more stark for high-value devices such as pacemakers, heart valves and intraocular lenses.

Article Title: Child abuse content row: Meta admits lapses, govt questions its 'safe harbour' status
Article Text:
Meta officials admitted to a mistake during their appearance before NCPCR

(With inputs from Aabhas Sharma)

NEW DELHI: Govt has told Meta that it cannot go on invoking intermediary status and must shoulder greater responsibility as a service provider after the tech giant admitted to lapses in dealing with child sexual abuse material. This can have far-reaching consequences, including the company losing the "safe harbour" immunity that it enjoys on grounds of being an intermediary, although it can challenge any decision of the govt in court.The tech giant admitted mistakes and assured the authorities that it would immediately report child sexual abuse material, persons in the know said.Govt has told Meta that it must shoulder greater responsibility following the tech giant admitting to lapses in dealing with child sexual abuse material. Officials said the company cannot go on invoking intermediary status. While adding it will risk losing the "safe harbour" immunity, govt also took the stand that the tech giant's recommendations to users and advertising systems give it responsibilities beyond that of an "intermediary" which is only hosting users' posts.Officials made it clear that Meta needed to remove child sexual abuse material that could drive children to suicide.NCPCR, too, warned the company's representatives when Meta India chief Arun Srinivas and senior executives appeared before the panel for its inquiry into alleged advertisements linked to child sexual exploitation and abuse material on the platform.The 70-minute meeting focused on safe harbour provisions under the IT Act, 2000, which offer intermediaries conditional protection from liability for third-party content, sources said. It is learnt NCPCR stressed upon Meta that this protection was "not absolute" but "relative" and depended on compliance with legal obligations, including reporting under the Pocso Act Sources said NCPCR did not accept Meta's arguments on the applicability of safe harbour provisions and pressed for evidence of compliance with IT Act, Pocso and Supreme Court's 2024 ruling on child sexual abuse material.NCPCR invoked the ruling to underline that intermediaries could not automatically claim protection under Sec 79 of IT Act in such cases. Meta faced a series of legal and technical questions, they added.Meta sought time to respond, and the commission granted it two weeks for answers to a questionnaire that would be shared with the company. NCPCR is likely to call company representatives for another hearing subsequently.The meeting was chaired by Valeti Premchand, additional secretary in WCD ministry, who holds charge as NCPCR chair. Representatives of MeitY and Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre were also part of the meeting, the sources said. Srinivas had not appeared on Sept 9 when he was first summoned. Other Meta executives who attended that meeting were told the commission would like to hear only from the India head of the company, in whose name the summons had been issued.
Article Summary: Govt has told Meta that it must shoulder greater responsibility as a service provider. The tech giant admitted to lapses in dealing with child sexual abuse material. This can have far-reaching consequences, including the company losing the "safe harbour" immunity that it enjoys.

It’s been almost two years now and that promise is nowhere,” Omar told reporters in Pulwama.On Sept 9, the MHA panel held latest round of talks with the Ladakhi delegation comprising representatives of Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) in New Delhi. A day after the meeting, the Ladakh administration said that Centre has agreed to constitute a union territory-level elected body for Ladakh under Article 371 of the Constitution and that the Centre has sought the views of Ladakhi representatives on the proposed body’s powers and its relationship with the existing Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils.“The subcommittee meeting, first of all, discussed the formation of a UT-level body under Article 371 of the Constitution, as decided in the previous meeting held on July 3. It was decided that a UT-level body will be formed under Article 371,” Ladakh chief secretary Asish Kundra said.Ladakhi representatives from LAB and KDA have been in talks with MHA since 2023 for constitutional safeguards covering land, jobs, culture and environment.The MHA had formed a committee on Jan 2, 2023, led by junior minister Nityanand Rai, to address key issues of Ladakh. Since then, several rounds of talks have been held.
Article Summary: J&K CM Omar Abdullah said Ladakhi representatives should not trust the Centre on any assurance until it is in writing. The CM also alleged that J&K was assured that the statehood would be restored, which wasn’t.

Article Title: Trump praises PM Modi for curbing ‘illicit opium cultivation’ as India stays on US ‘drug transit’ list
Article Text:
The US president also said Washington would continue working with New Delhi on counter-narcotics efforts (File photo)

US President Donald Trump on Wednesday welcomed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s efforts to curb illicit opium poppy cultivation in India, even as Washington included India among 23 countries designated as major drug transit or illicit drug-producing countries.In a Presidential Determination submitted to the US Congress, Trump said he looked forward to continued cooperation with India under the United States-India Drug Policy Framework. “I welcome Prime Minister Modi and the Government of India’s efforts to address illicit opium poppy cultivation and bolster supply chain integrity,” Trump said in the directive made public on Wednesday.India’s inclusion on the list does not, however, amount to a US finding that its government is failing to tackle the drug trade. The determination said countries are designated because of a combination of geographic, commercial and economic factors that allow illicit drugs or precursor chemicals to be produced or moved through their territory.The US document specifically noted that being placed on the list does not necessarily reflect a country’s current counterdrug efforts or the extent of its cooperation with Washington.Along with India, the countries identified by the US include Afghanistan, The Bahamas, Belize, Bolivia, Burma, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Jamaica, Laos, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Pakistan, Peru, Venezuela and China.The designation comes as Washington continues to focus on disrupting international drug supply chains, including the movement of precursor chemicals used to manufacture synthetic drugs. The White House’s 2026 National Drug Control Strategy has also called for stronger bilateral counterdrug cooperation with countries including India.Trump said the US and India would continue working together on counter-narcotics efforts. The two countries established a Drug Policy Executive Working Group earlier this year, with discussions focused on illicit narcotics trafficking, precursor chemicals and the security of pharmaceutical supply chains.The US president also pointed to what he described as “historic progress” by his administration in tackling drug trafficking and narcoterrorist organisations.He cited tighter border security, lower drug seizures and a decline in overdose deaths as evidence of progress, saying seizures of fentanyl and other drugs along the US southern border had fallen by more than half after what he called four years of “open border chaos”.“After four years of open border chaos, seizures of fentanyl and other drugs being smuggled into the United States have been reduced by more than half, and drug overdose deaths have plunged,” Trump said.Trump separately called on China to take stronger action against the flow of precursor chemicals used to manufacture fentanyl, methamphetamine and other synthetic drugs.“The PRC continues to be the world’s largest producer of many of the precursor chemicals used to illicitly produce fentanyl, methamphetamine, and other deadly synthetic drugs,” Trump said.He said he had raised the issue directly with Chinese President Xi Jinping and noted that Beijing had introduced licensing requirements last year for companies exporting designated precursor chemicals to North America.The US has made disruption of precursor-chemical supply chains a central part of its broader counter-drug strategy, which calls for international cooperation to prevent legitimate trade channels from being exploited for illicit drug production.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump welcomed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s efforts to curb illicit opium poppy cultivation in India. Washington included India among 23 countries designated as major drug transit or illicit drug-producing countries. Trump said the US and India would continue working together on counter-narcotics efforts.

Article Title: UPI charges row: Chidambaram among 5 Congress MPs who had backed revenue framework

NEW DELHI: As Rahul Gandhi stepped up his criticism of the government over the MDR announcement and demanded its rollback, calling it a “UPI tax”, a Standing Committee on Finance report had earlier emphasised the need for a viable revenue mechanism to ensure the UPI ecosystem remains financially sustainable without placing a perpetual burden on the government exchequer.The report was prepared by a committee that included Congress leaders, including former finance minister P Chidambaram.The Standing Committee on Finance, which includes Congress MPs such as P Chidambaram, Manish Tewari, Gaurav Gogoi, Kishori Lal and K Gopinath, in its report presented to Parliament on August 12 this year, called for a tiered MDR or revenue framework for UPI.The panel also said the framework should be notified and operationalised without delay.In its report, the Committee noted the “massive Rs. 2000 crore budgetary allocation for 2026-27 designed to offset ecosystem costs caused by the zero-MDR policy on RuPay and low-value UPI transactions”.The Committee observed that while UPI is projected to process up to 150 billion transactions a month and add 600 million new users, the current government incentive covers only 11% of the industry's actual costs and 14% of potential MDR collections.It said this creates a structural funding gap that could affect long-term investment in infrastructure.“The Committee would like to emphasize that establishing a viable revenue mechanism is critical to ensuring the UPI ecosystem achieves financial sustainability without perpetually straining the Government exchequer,” the report said, as cited by ANI.“In the view of the Committee, while statutory enablement now exists to permit calibrated MDR on high-value transactions, any delay in notifying and operationalizing this framework leaves payment service providers heavily dependent on inadequate subsidies, thereby threatening critical investments in cybersecurity, fraud prevention, and network infrastructure,” it added.The report, headed by BJP MP Bhartruhari Mahtab, was adopted by the panel, and no dissent was recorded in the published minutes, officials were quoted as saying by news agency ANI.The development comes as Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday attacked Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the Centre’s new Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework for Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions, accusing the government of yielding to pressure from the United States and urging Modi to “have a spine”.In a video posted on X, Gandhi referred to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi while comparing her stance with Modi’s approach to the new UPI measures. “Indiraji was once asked whether she leans left or right, and her response was, ‘I don't lean left or right. I stand straight’,” Gandhi said.He then turned to the new UPI framework, alleging that PM Modi had adopted a different approach.Meanwhile, the Centre has ruled out any rollback of the proposed 0.4 per cent Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions above Rs 2,000, saying the decision has already been taken and will come into effect from October 15.The government has clarified that the new UPI framework will have no impact on person-to-person transactions, which will continue to remain completely free, irrespective of the amount transferred.Payments to merchants of up to Rs 2,000, along with transactions covered under the zero-MDR framework for small merchants, will also remain free.The government also clarified that MDR is neither a tax nor a charge collected by the government or NPCI. Instead, it is distributed among payment ecosystem participants, including banks and payment application providers, to support the operation and continued expansion of the UPI ecosystem.
Article Summary: The Standing Committee on Finance called for a tiered MDR or revenue framework for UPI. The panel also said the framework should be notified and operationalised without delay. The development comes as Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi attacked Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the Centre’s new Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework.

Article Title: 'Govt can't subsidise everything': Niti Aayog VC's 'bees and honey' take on UPI charges
Article Text:
Businesses should bear modest UPI transaction costs, govt cannot subsidise everything: NITI Aayog VC Lahiri

NEW DELHI: NITI Aayog vice chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri on Wednesday defended the Centre’s decision to introduce a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on high-value UPI transactions, saying businesses must find ways to become self-sustaining rather than depend on government subsidies.Quoting ancient Indian teacher and philosopher Chanakya, Lahiri said a ruler should collect taxes from citizens as a bee collects honey from a flower — “gently, gradually, and without inflicting pain or bruising the petals”.“So you have to find ways of sustaining businesses without having to give subsidy,” Lahiri told reporters on the sidelines of an event, clarifying that this was his personal view and not NITI Aayog’s official position.The remarks came a day after the government announced that a 0.4 per cent MDR would apply from October 15 to UPI payments of more than Rs 2,000 made to merchants. Person-to-person transactions and small merchant payments will remain outside the levy.Also read: New UPI charges challenged in SC; petitioner flags impact on common man Lahiri sought to put the proposed charge in perspective, saying the impact on individual transactions would be limited.“Look at the numbers that is for Rs 100. You pay 40 paise for transaction worth Rs 100.That also on big transactions... Is that going to kill you? No, but you need to run businesses on a self-sustainable basis,” he said.He also compared the proposed charge with other banking services.“You will get used to it. For example, cheque books - when you take from banks, you pay a small amount for it. Does it pinch? It's part of the business,” Lahiri said.The move has drawn opposition from traders, shopkeepers and political parties, with critics referring to the proposed levy as a ‘Modi Tax’.Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had given in to US pressure over the change.“Modi ji has a completely different concept. He's neither left nor right; he has decided to lie down straight and prostrate himself in front of Donald Trump,” Gandhi said in a video message posted on X.“He's put a tax on every single Indian person by taxing UPI and giving a huge amount of money to the United States. Modi ji, please stop lying down in front of the United States. Have a spine, stand up and take back the UPI tax,” he added.The Congress has alleged that the government acted on a US demand to end the zero-MDR regime. The party also took a swipe at Modi, saying he had “redefined NOTA -- Narendra's Ongoing Trump Appeasement”.The finance ministry had earlier rejected the allegation of foreign influence, saying India’s UPI policy decisions were being made independently.“Some claims suggest the change is due to foreign influence. This is false. India’s UPI policy decisions are made independently, with the clear goal of building a self-sustaining, inclusive, and affordable digital payments ecosystem,” it said in a post on X.Government sources told news agency PTI that the MDR decision was taken in the larger interest of the UPI ecosystem and to strengthen its safety and security, and it cannot be rolled back. 'When decision has been taken, question of its rollback doesn't arise', he said.The proposed 0.4 per cent MDR will be paid by merchants and capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 or more. The government has ruled out a rethink, with a senior official telling PTI, “There is no question of a re-think.”The new regime is scheduled to take effect from October 15.
Article Summary: NITI Aayog vice chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri defended the Centre’s decision to introduce a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on high-value UPI transactions. He said businesses must find ways to become self-sustaining rather than depend on government subsidies. Lahiri said a ruler should collect taxes from citizens as a bee collects honey from a flower.

Article Title: From ‘Ankur’ to ‘Malgudi Days’, Anant Nag’s five-decade journey earns Phalke honour

NEW DELHI: Veteran actor Anant Nag , whose career spans Kannada cinema, Hindi films and the much-loved television series ‘Malgudi Days’, will receive the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024, the government announced on Wednesday, recognising more than five decades of work across languages.The 78-year-old actor will be presented with India’s highest cinema honour at the 72nd National Film Awards ceremony in Kevadia, Gujarat, on September 22, 2026. The recognition follows the Padma Bhushan conferred on him in 2025.Announcing the selection, the government said Nag’s cinematic journey had “inspired generations of artists and enriched the cultural landscape of the nation”. He was chosen on the recommendation of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award Selection Committee.Nag made his film debut with the Kannada feature ‘Sankalp’ and entered Hindi cinema with ‘Ankur’. Over a career that marked its golden jubilee in 2023, he has appeared in more than 300 films across Kannada, Hindi, Telugu, Malayalam, Tamil and Marathi. His television work includes ‘Malgudi Days’, adding another dimension to a career distinguished by its range of characters and languages.His honours include five Filmfare Awards and five Karnataka State Best Actor Awards, besides the Karnataka Rajyotsava Award and the state’s lifetime achievement award.Nag’s public life also extended beyond the screen. He served in the Karnataka Legislative Council from 1988 to 1994 and in the legislative assembly from 1994 to 1999. During his assembly tenure, he held office as minister of state for Bangalore city development.Instituted in 1969, with Devika Rani as its first recipient, the Dadasaheb Phalke Award recognises outstanding contributions to the growth and development of Indian cinema . It commemorates the filmmaker who directed ‘Raja Harishchandra’, India’s first full-length feature film, in 1913.The award carries a Swarna Kamal medallion, a shawl and a cash prize of Rs 10 lakh.
Article Summary: Anant Nag will receive the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024. The recognition follows the Padma Bhushan conferred on him in 2025. He has appeared in more than 300 films across Kannada, Hindi, Telugu, Malayalam, Tamil and Marathi.

Article Title: RML lab system non-functional two years after installation, patients continue to face delays

NEW DELHI: Patients at RML Hospital continue to face delays in getting blood and biopsy reports as the hospital's Laboratory Information System (LIS), installed in 2024, remains non-functional, forcing them to depend on the manual process of collecting physical reports.The LIS was meant to integrate laboratory services with the hospital's existing Hospital Information System (HIS). If functioning, reports would be available electronically, allowing patients to access them through the hospital system and doctors to view them directly, without patients having to return to the hospital or carry physical copies.The issue was flagged by The Times of India through a grievance filed on the Centre's CPGRAMS portal. The LIS had not been integrated with the existing HIS and approximately Rs 1 crore had been paid to the vendor, while no report had been generated through the system.Sources said the system was installed around two years ago at a cost exceeding Rs 1 crore, with 90% of the payment released to the vendor. The issue reportedly came up recently when the hospital director sought details of laboratory-test computerisation.The LIS was intended to integrate laboratory departments, including biochemistry, pathology and microbiology, with the hospital's existing system. However, the integration remains incomplete, with the biochemistry component also yet to be fully integrated, sources said.The system's continued non-functioning means its intended benefit of electronic access to laboratory reports for patients and doctors has not materialised even around two years after installation.The response to the CPGRAMS grievance did not address the functioning of the LIS. In a communication dated October 16, 2025, RML's grievance cell instead asked the complainant to confirm whether the complaint had been filed by them and submit related documents as evidence in support of the grievance.Responding to the issue, a senior RML Hospital administration official said, “Patient services have remained uninterrupted during the transition. Laboratory reports have continued to be provided under the existing operational system, while the LIS integration is nearing completion and is expected to go live shortly.”The hospital said the LIS was successfully interfaced with its eHospital platform in September 2025 and that, following NIC's recommendation to align the system with the forthcoming Next-Generation eHospital platform, the final integration is now being taken up on priority. The hospital said the Department of Biochemistry is expected to be the first to operationalise the upgraded LIS.
Article Summary: RML lab system non-functional two years after installation, patients continue to face delays. If functioning, reports would be available electronically, allowing patients to access them through the hospital system. The issue was flagged by The Times of India through a grievance filed on the Centre's CPGRAMS portal.

Article Title: CM Pushkar Singh Dhami attends 'Yuva Sankalp Diwas', urges youth to adopt three resolutions for developed Uttarakhand
Article Text:
CM Pushkar Singh Dhami attends 'Yuva Sankalp Diwas', urges youth to adopt three resolutions for developed Uttarakhand
