Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami participated in the "Yuva Sankalp Diwas" programme organised at Rangers Ground in Dehradun on Wednesday.On the occasion, the CM also visited the photo exhibition set up at the venue.Expressing his gratitude to the youth of the state for celebrating his birthday as "Yuva Sankalp Diwas", CM Dhami said that being among the young people on his birthday was the biggest gift for him. He said the energy, enthusiasm and determination of the youth continuously inspire and energise him. "In the eyes of the youth, I see the vision of a developed and self-reliant Uttarakhand," he said.The chief minister said that the youth would play a crucial role in realising Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of building a developed India by 2047.By 2047, when the country completes 100 years of Independence, today's youth will be leading the development of the country and the state across various sectors. He said the talent, hard work and innovation of the youth would be instrumental in realising the vision of a developed Uttarakhand as part of a developed India.CM Dhami said the youth of Uttarakhand are hardworking, talented, disciplined and capable of facing challenges.Providing them with the right direction, better opportunities and a transparent environment is a priority of the state government, he said.The government is continuously working to create new opportunities for the youth in every sector, from education and skill development to employment, self-employment, startups and sports, he added. He said the government's endeavour is to ensure that the youth of Uttarakhand do not have to leave their homes, villages or the state out of compulsion to pursue their dreams. "The youth should not only become job seekers but also job creators through entrepreneurship," he said.The Chief Minister said Artificial Intelligence, robotics, automation and digital technologies are rapidly transforming the nature of employment and industry. The state government is focusing on equipping young people with modern skills in line with future requirements, he said.He added that new self-employment opportunities are also being created through tourism, homestays and local products. To promote industrial development in the hill regions and generate employment at the local level, the government has decided to develop special industrial areas in Chamoli, Pauri and Almora districts.CM Dhami said the establishment of the State Youth Commission is an important step towards connecting the hopes and aspirations of young people with policymaking. The government wants to ensure the voice and participation of the youth in the formulation of policies concerning them, he said.The Youth Commission will play an important role in promoting skill development, employment, entrepreneurship and innovation, while also digitally empowering young people and creating awareness about drug abuse, cybercrime and other social evils, he added.The Chief Minister said Uttarakhand's youth are also bringing laurels to the state at the national and international levels in sports. Following the successful hosting of the 38th National Games, Devbhoomi Uttarakhand is also establishing a new identity as a sporting state, he said.The state government is continuously working to develop sports infrastructure and provide better opportunities to athletes, he added.CM Dhami said a stringent anti-copying law has been implemented in the state to ensure transparency in recruitment processes and safeguard the future of hardworking youth. He said the government is committed to ensuring that no young person faces injustice after years of hard work and that their dreams and rights are protected."No appointment is merely a number; behind every appointment lies the hard work of a young person and the hopes of their family," he said.The Chief Minister called upon the youth to set ambitious goals and work with dedication to achieve them. Referring to Swami Vivekananda's message, "Arise, awake and do not stop until the goal is achieved," he urged young people to make hard work a habit, discipline their identity and make the desire to learn a part of their lives.He also called upon the youth to use technology and mobile phones positively, saying digital platforms should be used not only for entertainment but also for enhancing knowledge and skills. In the age of social media, he urged young people to remain cautious about incomplete and misleading information and to verify every piece of information against facts.Expressing concern over the growing trend of drug abuse among young people, CM Dhami said addiction not only weakens the body but also affects a person's dreams and future. "The hands that should hold books and skills should not hold drugs," he said.He urged the youth to stay away from drugs themselves and encourage their friends and people around them to do the same.On his birthday, the Chief Minister asked the youth to give him a "bouquet of three resolutions." He urged them to first set a major goal in life and work hard with full dedication to achieve it; secondly, stay away from drugs and help their peers do the same; and thirdly, once they achieve success in their chosen fields, contribute a part of their knowledge, experience and abilities towards the development of Uttarakhand.CM Dhami said whether young people become doctors, engineers, scientists, sportspersons, teachers, entrepreneurs or join public service, they must first become good human beings and responsible citizens.He expressed confidence that the dreams, hard work and determination of Uttarakhand's youth would lay a strong foundation for building a developed Uttarakhand as part of a developed India.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami attended 'Yuva Sankalp Diwas' He urged youth to adopt three resolutions for developed Uttarakhand. He said the youth would play a crucial role in realising Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of building a developed India by 2047.

Article Title: Not Mumbai, not Delhi: This North Indian city tops India in domestic expenditure
Article Text:
As per the study, an average household in Chandigarh spends nearly Rs 19 lakh annually.

Chandigarh has the highest average household spending in India

The report identifies Chandigarh as a Frontier city, a category comprising the smaller urban centres among India's top 100 cities by population.

Chandigarh and Bengaluru have the highest average household income

Delhi NCR: India’s biggest urban consumption market

Delhi NCR’s transportation spending alone is bigger than some cities

Mumbai: More high-income households, but not the highest average spending

Bengaluru: Highest average income, but Chandigarh leads consumption

Big Six: Cities with populations above 10 million.

Boomtowns: Cities with populations between 2.5 million and 10 million.

Breakout cities: Cities with populations between 1.5 million and 2.5 million.

Frontier cities: Cities with populations between 0.5 million and 1.5 million.

Chandigarh has emerged as India's highest-spending city on a per-household basis, according to The Many Urban Indias , a report by People’s Research on India’s Consumer Economy (PRICE) and Tata Sons. An average household in the city spends nearly Rs 19 lakh a year, putting Chandigarh ahead of India's biggest metropolitan centres on this measure. The study examines how households across India’s 100 leading cities earn, spend, save and borrow.Chandigarh is identified as the city with the highest average household consumption in the report. As per the study, an average household in Chandigarh spends nearly Rs 19 lakh annually. The distinction is about average spending per household, not the total amount spent across the entire city. This matters because larger cities have many more households and can generate a much bigger overall consumer market even when their average household spending is lower.The report identifies Chandigarh as a Frontier city, a category comprising the smaller urban centres among India's top 100 cities by population.It places the city among the country's highest-spending urban centres, alongside Thiruvananthapuram in Kerala. The report also highlights Chandigarh's household financial position, noting that it has high levels of savings and low levels of debt.Chandigarh’s spending figures become more interesting when viewed alongside household income. According to the study, Bengaluru and Chandigarh have the highest average household income in India, at Rs 28 lakh per year. India's six largest metropolitan centres- Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata and Hyderabad are grouped together as the Big Six in the study. They have more than 10 million people each and account for a substantial share of the country's urban economic activity.Delhi NCR is a major part of the report’s consumption story. The study says that Delhi NCR has a total consumption market worth $126 billion. This is nearly as much as Mumbai and Bengaluru combined. The report attributes this to two factors: Delhi NCR has around 7.5 million households, compared with 4.6 million in Mumbai. Its average annual household consumption is nearly Rs 15 lakh. This gives Delhi NCR a large overall consumption market, even though Chandigarh leads on average household spending.One of the report’s more striking findings concerns transportation. Delhi NCR households spend more than $33 billion annually on transportation, according to the study. That amount is larger than the total consumption market of Pune or Ahmedabad. The report also estimates that Delhi NCR’s annual dairy consumption is around $10 billion.Mumbai remains one of India’s major consumption centres, but the report places it behind Chandigarh on average household spending. The study says that Amritsar, Ahmedabad and Jabalpur have higher average household spending than Mumbai. At the same time, Mumbai leads the 100-city group in the share of high-income households.The report defines high-income households as those earning more than Rs 36 lakh annually at 2025-26 prices. Their share across the 100 cities has increased to 12%, from 3% a decade earlier.Bengaluru is another important comparison in the report. The city shares the highest average household income position with Chandigarh, at Rs 28 lakh per year. However, the report says that Chandigarh and Thiruvananthapuram have the highest average household consumption in India. It also identifies Surat as a city where average household consumption is higher than Bengaluru’s. This means Bengaluru’s high average income does not automatically translate into the highest average household spending.The report groups the cities into four categories:Chandigarh falls in the Frontier category, while Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru are part of the Big Six.
Article Summary: Chandigarh has emerged as India's highest-spending city on a per-household basis, according to The Many Urban Indias report. An average household in the city spends nearly Rs 19 lakh a year, putting it ahead of India's biggest metropolitan centres on this measure. The study examines how households across India’s 100 leading cities earn, spend, save and borrow. Delhi NCR has a total consumption market worth $126 billion.

Article Title: 'Meta has admitted mistake, must remove child abuse content': Govt sources say firm has no immunity
Article Text:
Meta admits mistake, to alert authorities on child sexual abuse material

NEW DELHI: Meta has admitted to a mistake and will immediately inform authorities about material related to child sexual abuse.Sources said that Meta will have to remove content related to the sexual abuse of children and material that could lead people to suicide.The government has told Meta that it can no longer be treated only as an intermediary but as a service provider, and will have to take responsibility for the content and services it provides. The development could have far-reaching consequences for Meta, sources added.The government believes Meta may no longer be entitled to legal immunity, although the issue will ultimately have to be decided by a court, they said.The development comes as Meta said it will report child-safety matters directly to India's National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, amid heightened government scrutiny over allegations that paid advertisements linked to child sexual abuse material (CSAM) appeared on Instagram.Until now, Meta primarily routed child-safety reports through the US-based National Center for Missing and Exploited Children. The new commitment will establish a direct reporting channel to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, managed by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the Ministry of Home Affairs.The Centre described the move as a first step and stressed that "much more" needs to be done. "Online safety of children is a fundamental principle for any social media platform to operate in India and it is non-negotiable," officials said.The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) first issued a notice to Meta on July 3, 2026, seeking an explanation over advertisements allegedly linked to child sexual abuse material (CSEAM). Meta submitted its response a week later.The Commission subsequently decided to institute a formal inquiry to establish the facts of the matter and summoned Meta's India managing director and head to appear before it.The Meta head did not appear at the September 9 hearing, with the company instead represented by senior executives. Meta officials cited urgent reasons for the senior executive's absence, following which the NCPCR directed that the company's India head appear at the next hearing.
Article Summary: The government has told Meta that it can no longer be treated only as an intermediary but as a service provider. The development could have far-reaching consequences for Meta, sources added. Meta will have to remove content related to the sexual abuse of children and material that could lead people to suicide.

Article Title: Centre declares Pak-based Shahzad Bhatti Network a terrorist organisation under UAPA
Article Text:
Amit Shah said the Centre has declared the Pakistan-based SBN a terrorist organisation

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Wednesday said the Centre has declared the Pakistan-based Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN) a terrorist organisation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).He said the decision was taken in keeping with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of adopting a zero-tolerance approach towards terrorism."The group is involved in smuggling of arms, explosives and narcotics across borders, apart from inciting youths and petty criminals into terrorism. Targeting India's democratic structure and the fabric of communal harmony, the syndicate also published hateful digital content," Shah said in a post on X.A gazette notification issued by the Union Home Ministry on Wednesday invoked Section 35(1)(a) of the UAPA to add "Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN)" to the First Schedule of the Act, which lists organisations designated as terrorist groups.The Centre said the action was taken based on its assessment that SBN was involved in "terrorism and has participated in various acts of terrorism in India.""'Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN)' is an organisation whose objective is to involve gullible youth and local criminals to smuggle arms, explosives, and narcotics from across the border, and through terrorist activities, pose a serious threat to the democratic system, communal harmony, and internal security of the country," the notification said.The notification cited criminal cases registered against alleged SBN members under laws including the UAPA, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Arms Act, Explosives Act, Information Technology Act and Prevention of Defacement of Property Act.The notification cited criminal cases against alleged SBN members under laws including the UAPA, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Arms Act, Explosives Act, Information Technology Act and Prevention of Defacement of Property Act.It said the SBN was involved in "radicalising gullible youth" through various allurements, motivating them to engage in anti-national activities and mobilising resources for such acts in collusion with other banned outfits and similarly designated entities."And whereas, the 'Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN)' is promoting terrorism through violent activities that disrupt public order and by using various digital communication platforms to disseminate provocative messages, posing a serious challenge to the integrity of the nation," the notification read.The move comes nearly a month after a coordinated operation was carried out across 14 states to disrupt the SBN terror network and thwart its plans for subversive attacks ahead of Independence Day. The operation resulted in 253 detentions and more than 200 arrests, with over 80 FIRs registered against alleged SBN operatives.The ministry of home affairs (MHA) said on August 12 that the multi-state operation was conducted in coordination with state police forces using a real-time intelligence-sharing system. The 253 detentions included 62 in Uttar Pradesh, 52 in Haryana, 51 in Delhi, 44 in Punjab, 15 in Rajasthan, eight in Maharashtra, five in Uttarakhand, three each in Karnataka, Gujarat and Bihar, and two each in Telangana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Kerala. Fresh FIRs were registered in Delhi and Karnataka.According to the MHA, SBN, described as a Pakistan-based ISI-backed terror syndicate, is linked to grenade, IED and petrol bomb attacks and targeted killings across India. The group has also been accused of paying local conduits to conduct reconnaissance of police, defence and religious sites and install CCTV cameras for espionage.Under the UAPA, inclusion in the First Schedule formally designates an organisation as "terrorist" under Indian law. With the latest addition, SBN becomes the 46th organisation on the list.
Article Summary: Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN) is a Pakistan-based ISI-backed terror syndicate. The group is involved in smuggling of arms, explosives and narcotics across borders. The move comes nearly a month after a coordinated operation was carried out across 14 states to disrupt the SBN.

Article Title: Spate of deaths: Pilots body ask govt to end exemptions to airline on their duty norms
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Following a spate of unfortunate deaths of Indian pilots on duty or duty-related activities in less than three years, the Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) has asked the aviation ministry and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) to end all dispensations given to airlines from flight duty time limitation (FDTL) regulations. It has also sought an investigation into recent pilot fatalities.“…deeply concerned about increasing evidence of fatigue-related operational risks; the continued deferment and dilution of certain FDTL provisions through operator-specific dispensations, and the recent pilot fatalities that have heightened concerns regarding cumulative fatigue… and pilot well-being. While FIP does not seek to establish any direct link between fatigue and the individual fatalities, these events warrant an urgent and comprehensive review of fatigue exposure, rostering practices, recovery opportunities, medical surveillance, and fatigue risk management system (FRMS) effectiveness across Indian aviation operations,” FIP president Captain C S Randhawa has said in a mail to the aviation authorities sent on Tuesday.The federation has sought “immediate withdrawal of FDTL dispensations granted to operators in the interest of aviation safety; uniform implementation of all approved FDTL provisions; establishment of a DGCA-led national FRMS oversight programme; mandatory quarterly fatigue-reporting and FRMS performance submissions by operators; independent scientific review of pilot health trends and fatigue-related medical events and formal participation of pilot representative bodies in future FDTL and FRMS deliberations.In Nov 2023, an Air India pilot had died at Delhi Airport terminal 3. In Feb 2024, an Indian pilot working for Qatar Airways took ill on a Delhi-Doha flight while travelling as operating crew member and subsequently died. In April 2026, a pilot each of Air India and Akasa died. Last week, an AI pilot died in his Delhi hotel room during a layover.Big Indian airlines have managed to get multiple dispensations from FDTL norms that govern the duty hours of operating crew and their minimum rest along with the number of light landings they can safely perform. While these rules are for ensuring safety, airlines have managed dispensation by citing lack of crew that will impact their schedules.Struggling to survive in what is the most difficult period post Covid with oil prices spiking since the Iran-US war broke out this Feb and the rupee crashing amid continuing geopolitical challenges like airspace closures, airlines have so far managed to get a sympathetic view on dispensations they seek from FDTL norms. But a spate of unfortunate deaths now has alarm bells ringing in pilot circles and they want the aviation ministry/DGCA to act before more aviators lose their lives.
Article Summary: The Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) has asked the aviation ministry to end all dispensations given to airlines from flight duty time limitation (FDTL) regulations. It has also sought an investigation into recent pilot fatalities. Big Indian airlines have managed to get multiple dispensations from FDTL norms that govern the duty hours of operating crew.

Article Title: India-Pakistan naval ships collide in Arabian Sea: What 1991 pact says
Article Text:

India-Pakistan 1991 pact: What does it say

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday said the conduct of a Pakistani naval ship that led to a collision with an Indian Navy vessel in international waters was in direct contravention of Article 10 of a 1991 bilateral agreement between the two countries.India conveyed strong protest over the incident to Pakistan's Charge d'Affaires.“The Charge d'Affaires of the High Commission for the Islamic Republic of Pakistan in New Delhi was summoned to the ministry of external affairs today and a strong protest was lodged with him over the unacceptable and unprofessional conduct of Pakistani naval units at sea that led to a collision with a unit of the Indian Navy,” the ministry said in a statement."While the incident, which took place in international waters, did not cause any major damage, the conduct of the Pakistani naval ship was in direct contravention of Article 10 of the Agreement between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Manoeuvres and Troops Movements of April 1991," it added.The ministry further said that it advised the Pakistani diplomat "to convey to the concerned Pakistani authorities the need for all military units to observe due care and respect the provisions of the relevant agreements between the two sides in order to prevent any repeat of such incidents.""The Charge d'Affaires of India in Islamabad has also been instructed to lodge a similar protest with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan," it said.According to agency sources, a Pakistani naval ship came close to a frontline Indian Navy warship during a routine surveillance mission in the North Arabian Sea."The Pakistani vessel was travelling at high speed and manoeuvring in an “unprofessional and unsafe manner,” ANI reported quoting sources.The pact between Islamabad and Delhi was signed in April 1991 as part of a series of confidence-building measures between both countries. The measures were aimed at fostering trust and preventing accidental or unintended military confrontations.Under the agreement, the land, naval and air forces of both countries are to avoid major exercises close to each other. If such exercises are conducted within specified areas, the main force cannot be directed towards the other side and there should be no logistical build-up close to it.Under this pact, both nations agreed to provide notification to each other about significant military exercises, manoeuvres and troop movements near the border."Their Land, Naval and Air Forces will avoid holding major military manoeuvres and exercises in close proximity to each other. However if such exercises are held within distances as prescribed in this Agreement, the strategic direction of the main force being exercised will not be towards the other side, nor will any logistics build up be carried out close to it," the agreement says.Article 10 of the agreement says that naval ships and submarines of both countries have to maintain a distance of three Nautical Miles from each other."The Naval ships and submarines belonging to the other country are not to close less than three Nautical Miles (NMs) from each other so as to avoid any accident while operating in international waters," it says.Along with the 1991 agreement, New Delhi and Islamabad also committed themselves under the Memorandum of Understanding signed at Lahore on February 21, 1999, to conclude a “Prevention of Incidents at Sea” agreement to ensure the safety of navigation by their naval vessels and aircraft.The provision formed part of the Lahore confidence-building process and reflected the two countries’ intention to establish arrangements to prevent accidents and dangerous encounters at sea.
Article Summary: India conveyed strong protest over the incident to Pakistan's Charge d'Affaires. The Pakistani vessel was travelling at high speed and manoeuvring in an “unprofessional and unsafe manner,” sources said. The pact between Islamabad and Delhi was signed in April 1991 as part of a series of confidence-building measures.

Article Title: 'Have a spine, don't lie down in front of Trump': Rahul flays PM Modi over 'UPI tax'
Article Text:
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday attacked Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the Centre’s new Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework for Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions, accusing the government of yielding to pressure from the United States and urging Modi to “have a spine”.In a video posted on X, Rahul referred to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi while drawing a comparison with PM Modi over the new UPI measures.“Indiraji was once asked whether she leans left or right, and her response was, ‘I don't lean left or right. I stand straight’,” Gandhi said. He then turned to the UPI framework, alleging that Modi had adopted a different approach.“Modiji has a completely diff concept, he's neither left or right he has decided to completely lie down straight and in front of Donald Trump. He's put a tax on every single Indian person by taxing UPI and giving huge amount op money to the United States,” the former Congress president added.He said, “Modiji, please stop lying down in front of the US. Have a spine, stand up and withdraw the UPI tax. Thank you."The Congress has described the new MDR as a “Modi tax” and alleged that the decision was linked to pressure from the US. The party has also criticised the government’s handling of the policy, calling it another example of what general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh termed a “FAST (First Announce, Subsequently Think) move”.Ramesh earlier questioned the timing of the decision, saying, “Decision Making in Modi Govt -- Aug 6: Hon'ble Finance Minister says 'no decision has been taken on MDR'. Aug 10: FM in Parliament says 'No MDR framework has yet been finalised'. Sep 14: Notification is issued. Within 24 hrs, MDR charges introduced.”Earlier in the day, the finance ministry rejected allegations of foreign pressure behind the revised UPI framework, clarifying that changes in regulations stem entirely from domestic priorities. It said UPI said MDR would apply only to specified merchant transactions above Rs 2,000, while person-to-person UPI payments would remain free. Around 96 per cent of person-to-merchant transactions will remain unaffected.Under the framework, a 0.4 per cent MDR will apply to specified merchant payments above Rs 2,000 from October 15, capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. The charge is payable within the merchant-payment ecosystem, not by consumers.A flat Rs 5 charge will apply to utility bill payments, fuel purchases, insurance premiums, railway tickets and several government services.The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has said the revenue will support infrastructure resilience, cybersecurity, fraud prevention, innovation and customer service. UPI processed 24,508.96 million transactions worth nearly Rs 29.82 lakh crore in August 2026, according to NPCI data.The new framework is set to take effect from October 15, putting the focus on how merchants, banks and payment platforms absorb the revised costs and whether the change affects pricing or the wider adoption of digital payments.
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi attacks PM Narendra Modi over the Centre’s new Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework for Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions. Gandhi accuses the government of yielding to pressure from the United States and urging Modi to “have a spine”

Article Title: Punjab minister Arora meets UAEIIC secretary general, pitches state as next investment hotspot for UAE capital
Article Text:
Punjab Minister Arora meets UAEIIC Secretary General, pitches state as next investment hotspot for UAE capital. (Photo: ANI)

CHANDIGARH: In a major outreach to attract global capital and boost industrial development as envisioned by Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, Punjab Industries and Commerce Minister Aman Arora on Monday met Abdulla Ahmed Al Suwaidi, Secretary General of the UAE International Investment Council (UAEIIC), on the sidelines of the Annual Investment Meeting (AIM) in Dubai to discuss expansive opportunities for mobilising investments into the state.According to the Information and Public Relations Department, Punjab, during the meeting, the Industries Minister discussed Punjab’s vast economic potential with Abdulla Ahmed Al Suwaidi and invited UAE investors to tap into high-growth sectors through government, semi-government and private sector partnerships.Reiterating the state government’s resolve, Arora assured the UAEIIC of complete administrative support, handholding and logistical facilitation from the Punjab Government for global enterprises seeking to set up or expand operations in the state. He emphasised that under the visionary leadership of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, Punjab is keen to build long-term, mutually beneficial partnerships with UAE-based investors and institutional funds.Highlighting the state’s investor-centric reforms, the Minister underscored the ease of doing business facilitated through ‘Invest Punjab’—the state’s unified single-window platform that delivers prompt statutory approvals and clearances to ensure a smooth, hassle-free investment journey.“Punjab offers a highly conducive entrepreneurial ecosystem, excellent multimodal connectivity, skilled technical manpower, and a transparent governance framework. We invite UAE business leaders to become active partners in Punjab’s transformative economic growth story,” Arora said.The UAE UAEIIC, which unites the UAE’s public and private entities to channel outward foreign direct investment (FDI), welcomed the state delegation's proactive outreach. The engagement focused on establishing robust institutional linkages to enable direct capital inflows and joint ventures between the UAE and Punjab, the Public Relations Department said.Expressing confidence in the discussions, Arora noted that this engagement marks a significant milestone that will pave the way for deeper bilateral economic cooperation, stronger business ties and substantial investment pipelines in Punjab.
Article Summary: Punjab Industries and Commerce Minister Aman Arora met Abdulla Ahmed Al Suwaidi, Secretary General of the UAE International Investment Council. Arora assured the UAEIIC of complete administrative support, handholding and logistical facilitation from the Punjab Government.
